agent_notes: The Hebrew numbers the superscription as verse 1 (and verse 2 as the historical note); the KJV leaves both unnumbered (52:0) and begins at 52:1 with Hebrew verse 3. Every KJV number in this psalm is therefore Hebrew minus 2.

lamnatzeach is glossed 'to the choirmaster' following the STEPBible gloss and the tradition of the chief musician; the exact duty of the office (leader, director, 'for the overseer', as YLT) is uncertain. maskil is left transliterated in the gloss, with 'skilful poem / instruction' as a probable sense; the Targum reads 'good insight'.

ki asita ('for you have done') has no stated object; I leave it open in the literal layer and in the dramatic one, though Radak, Ibn Ezra and Meiri take it to mean the judgment on Doeg. Meiri notes the perfect stands for a future. 'it is good' in the last colon: the subject of tov is shimkha, 'your name' (so ASV, KJV), not the praise; BBE reads otherwise.

agent_notes: Revised per the reviewer: the added line 'You, who think the day is yours' is removed from the dramatic layer, so 'every hour of the day' belongs only to God's faithful love. The Hebrew kol-hayyom has no verb, and its reach (the chesed, or the boasting, as Malbim and Ibn Ezra's 'hasar kaf' reading allow) is a known ambiguity; the dramatic layer follows the majority reading, the chesed.

history.note: [should_fix] Remove 'You, who think the day is yours.' from translation_dramatic, so that 'every hour of the day' stays attached to God's faithful love only. (PS.52.3: 'מַה־תִּתְהַלֵּל בְּרָעָה הַגִּבּוֹר חֶסֶד אֵל כָּל־הַיּוֹם' ('the chesed of God [is] all the day'))

agent_notes: 'oseh remiyyah is ambiguous: it can describe the razor (YLT, ASV, KJV, 'working deceit') or address Doeg (vocative). I chose the vocative 'O doer of deceit' because the participle is masculine and the STEPBible gloss reads it so; lashon is common gender, so this is a judgment call. The packet's Targum and Radak/Meiri treat the razor as the deceitful one.

agent_notes: The form RA' is written with a dagesh in resh (reading 'ra'), a known pointing oddity that STEPBible flags; it is simply 'evil'. min-tov and min-dabber are comparative min ('more than'), as all five English versions render.

agent_notes: Revised per the reviewer: gloss 8 is now 'and he will uproot you' (Piel perfect with waw-consecutive sense, object suffix), matching Rashi's reading of a verb. The yachtekha note now attributes to Meiri only 'break you' (Jer 1:17) and, as an opinion he reports, 'burn you' (Prov 25:22); 'snatch up' is given as the lexical (STEPBible) sense. The verb is rare and disputed; the dramatic layer renders it 'seize', staying close to that lexical sense.

agent_notes: ma'uzzo (Radak notes its doubled zayin) comes from the same root as ya'oz, 'be strong', so 'refuge' and 'took strength' form a wordplay I keep. behavvato is the same noun hawwah as in verse 4; the KJV's 'wickedness' here and 'mischiefs' there hides that the psalmist repeats a word. I keep 'ruin' in both, though Rashi and Radak read 'wickedness'. BBE's 'in his wealth' follows a different reading that I do not adopt.
